title: Finite-map approximation on profinite spaces
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological space, where totally disconnected means that every connected subset has at most one point, and let $V$ be any topological space. Let $f:X\to V$ be continuous. If $S\subseteq V\times V$ contains an open neighbourhood of the diagonal $\{(v,v):v\in V\}$, then there exist an integer $n\geq0$, a continuous map $g:X\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to that finite set with its discrete topology, and a function $h:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to V$ such that $(f(x),h(g(x)))\in S$ for every $x\in X$. The empty space $X$ is allowed.
